5 Budget Hotels

heroSub: Five budget stays in Sriracha town that we've already reviewed in depth — a roomy apartment with a kitchen, a boutique residence with a rooftop pool, a seafront hotel with Koh Loy views, and a small stay with a soaking tub within walking distance of the mall. Every one sits in the town centre, walkable to Pacific Park, Robinson and Japanese restaurants. From around ฿650–900/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews at every stay
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of budget stays are there in Sriracha, and how do you pick the right one for your reason for coming?
introHtml: Sriracha isn't a beach-holiday town like Pattaya or Bang Saen, and that's exactly what makes choosing a budget stay here different — most people staying in Sriracha town come for "work reasons" rather than for a holiday, whether that's working in the Eastern industrial estates, heading in and out of Laem Chabang port, running errands in town, or using it as a base for day trips to Pattaya. The town is also home to one of the largest Japanese communities in the country, so the area around these stays is full of ramen shops, izakaya and Japanese-style supermarkets. Budget stays in Sriracha town come in several types: some are roomy apartments with a kitchen for cooking your own meals, good for long stays; some are boutique residences with a rooftop pool and gym on a light budget; some are seafront hotels where you open the balcony to a Koh Loy view; and some are small stays with a soaking tub a few steps from the mall. Plenty of people book a budget stay and end up disappointed because they expected a sea view or a pool the place simply doesn't have. This article rounds up 5 budget stays in Sriracha town that we've already reviewed in depth — every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, and giving you the direct booking links, so you can pick the stay that really fits your reason for coming.
mrtHtml: Sriracha has no metro, and public transport in town isn't frequent. Driving yourself is the most convenient, because most of the stays in this article have free parking (except Benri, which uses public parking, and Seaview, where parking is about 200 m from the building). If you don't have a car, you can still get a ride-hailing app in town and many stays will help call a taxi. The stay areas in this article: Surasak sub-district — the side near Pacific Park and Robinson Sriracha, walkable to the malls and restaurants (Racha Residence, Triple B). Town centre, Surasak Sa-nguan–Sriracha Nakhon roads — near the market, the pier and Surasak Montri Park, with a walk along the seafront to Koh Loy (Cityview, Benri). Seafront, Choemchonphon road — open the balcony to Koh Loy, walkable to the pier for Koh Sichang (Seaview). Driving from Bangkok via the motorway or Sukhumvit road takes about an hour and a half to two hours. Pattaya is about a 20–30 min drive for anyone who wants to extend the trip to the beach.

entries.name: Racha Residence
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · roomy, with a kitchen
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Surasak sub-district · in town · near Pacific Park
entries.storyHtml: Among Sriracha's budget stays, if you go by overall score, Racha Residence is the one that does it best in this article — 8.7 from over 634 real reviews on Trip.com. It's an 8-storey apartment hotel in Surasak sub-district, in the centre of Sriracha town, open since 2014 with around 100 rooms. The point people bring up most is that the rooms are larger than the price suggests and every one has a kitchenette with a fridge, hob, range hood, sofa and dining corner — you can live comfortably, like at home, from a Superior of about 30 sqm up to a two-bedroom Executive of 68 sqm that suits a whole family. Real reviews agree the rooms are spacious, well equipped, the water pressure is good, and it feels more like a comfortable apartment than an ordinary hotel room. There's an 8th-floor rooftop you can go up to for the breeze and the sunset, a free gym, and roomy free parking, which works for anyone driving themselves or coming to work in the industrial zone. Breakfast offers Japanese options like curry rice and yaki udon alongside Western dishes, reflecting Sriracha's Japanese-community character. The in-town location is about a 15-minute walk to Pacific Park and Robinson, with a convenience store across from the stay. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building has been open since 2014 and some rooms are starting to show their age, with the occasional review mentioning a musty smell or cleanliness in spots, and some rooms picking up noise from next door. There's no pool here, and it isn't on the water, so there's no full sea view. This isn't the pick for anyone after a luxury beachfront resort, but it's the best value per room size for anyone who wants a homey feel, an in-room kitchen and a long stay in Sriracha town on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're sensitive to wear or musty smells, ask for a recently renovated or higher-floor room, and check the room's condition at check-in — if you're not happy you can ask to move. For a long stay of a week or a month, ask the property directly about the monthly rate, which works out better than booking nightly.

Score of 8.7, the highest in this article, from over 634 real reviews

entries.name: Triple B Boutique Residence
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Surasak sub-district · ~400 m walk to Robinson
entries.storyHtml: If you go by the number of reviews, Triple B Boutique Residence is the one with the most in this article — over 1,300 real reviews on Trip.com, with a high-8 score of 8.6. It's a compact boutique residence of about 47 rooms in Surasak sub-district, in the centre of Sriracha town, leaning more towards clean and simple than luxurious. What real reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are clean and larger than the price, the beds are especially comfortable, the bathrooms are big, and the air-con cools well — many rooms have a balcony and a large TV with Netflix. There's a range from Standard up to a Deluxe Studio with both a double and a single bed, good for three. The location is another strong point: it's about 400 m, or under 10 minutes, on foot to Robinson Sriracha and Pacific Park, surrounded by ramen shops, Japanese restaurants and convenience stores, so you don't need a car for every meal. For the price it still gives you good facilities — a rooftop pool with a sun terrace, a gym, free parking, and 24-hour check-in, handy for shift workers or late arrivals. What makes it especially good value for long stays is a monthly rate from around ฿7,000 a month. Honest caveats from the reviews: the rooftop pool is fairly small, better for a soak and a chill than serious swimming; the Thai breakfast like rice porridge is tasty but the Western options are few and some meals aren't served hot; it's a stay in the middle of an industrial town with some traffic noise; and the English-language TV channels are limited. In short, it's the best value for room quality per price — good for Laem Chabang workers, monthly guests, and anyone who just wants a good room, a good bed and a walk to the mall.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're a light sleeper, ask for a higher-floor room or one that doesn't face the main road when you book. For a brighter room with a balcony, specify a Deluxe Double or Deluxe Twin. For a long stay, ask the property directly about the monthly rate — it works out far better than booking nightly.

entries.name: Seaview Sriracha Hotel
entries.revCount: Around 8.6 on average · over 426 real reviews
entries.badge: 🌊 The only one with a Koh Loy view
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Seafront, Choemchonphon rd · walkable to Koh Loy
tags: ⛴️ Walkable to the Koh Sichang pier
entries.storyHtml: Among Sriracha's budget stays, Seaview Sriracha Hotel is the only one selling what the others don't — a sea view. It's a compact seafront hotel of about 60 rooms on Choemchonphon road, on the water in the centre of Sriracha town, open since around 2005 and refurbished in 2020. The point many people mention is that many rooms have a private balcony where you open the door to the sea and the silhouette of Koh Loy floating in the bay, at prices starting in the low thousands — not easy to find for a sea-view room in town. What surprises reviewers is that the rooms here are larger than the price and well stocked — many have a fridge (some even two), a microwave, a kettle, crockery, a sofa and a sitting corner, more like a small suite than an ordinary hotel room. The seafront location is the highlight: it's a short walk to Koh Loy, Sriracha market and the pier for Koh Sichang, ideal for anyone planning to take the boat over to Koh Sichang on a morning-to-evening day trip. The service is what gets the most consistent praise — the staff are friendly and kind, and some reviews got a room upgrade to a higher floor without asking. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no pool and no in-house gym; on some nights you hear noise from next door and music from festivals on Koh Loy; some furniture and fittings are starting to age with the building; and parking is about 200 m from the building. It's best for anyone who values sleeping right by the sea in town at a budget price, a roomy room and a walk to Koh Loy, more than luxury and resort-style facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you really want a sea and Koh Loy view, specify a Sea View Balcony room and ask for a higher floor when you book, since the view from upper floors is far more open than from lower ones. If you're a light sleeper, ask whether there's a festival on Koh Loy during your stay, and ask for a room on the side that doesn't face the stage.

entries.name: Benri Sriracha Residence
entries.badge: 💰 Cheapest in the article · has a soaking tub
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sriracha Nakhon rd Soi 1 · 2-min walk to Pacific Park
entries.addr: 1-3 Sriracha Nakhon Road Soi 1, Sriracha, Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If the brief is price, Benri Sriracha Residence is the one that starts cheapest in this article, at around ฿650/night. It's a small residence of about 10 rooms on the second floor of a commercial building, on Sriracha Nakhon road Soi 1, in the heart of Sriracha's business and shopping district. The biggest draw is the location — about a 2-minute walk to the Pacific Park mall and Robinson Sriracha, so you barely have to plan around food and supplies, and the area around it is the Japanese community, full of ramen shops, izakaya and sushi within easy walking distance. What real reviews praise most is that the rooms are clean and the beds and pillows are softer and comfier than the price, scoring especially high on cleanliness. There's a range from a Smart Studio of about 30 sqm up to a Deluxe Room of about 40 sqm, and what sets Benri apart from an ordinary guesthouse is that many rooms have a kitchenette with a fridge and a soaking tub in the bathroom for a Japanese-style soak to ease the day, which fits this neighbourhood and isn't easy to find at this price. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay is on the second floor and the building's sign isn't clear, so first-timers may not find the entrance straight away; there's no private car park, so you use the public parking beside the building; staff are only on site during business hours, so let them know your check-in time in advance if you're arriving early or late; and there's no pool or gym. It's best for solo travellers and couples focused on value, Laem Chabang workers who want a small base in town, and anyone shopping or running errands who wants to stay near the mall.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: let them know your check-in time clearly in advance, since staff are only on site during business hours. The stay is on the second floor and the sign isn't clear, so use the Sriracha Nakhon road Soi 1 pin near Pacific Park as your anchor, and call for directions if you can't find it. For a long stay or if you like cooking your own meals, make sure the room you book has a kitchenette and a fridge.

entries.name: Cityview Residence
entries.badge: 🛁 Shower & bathroom nicer than the price
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Surasak Sa-nguan road · centre of Sriracha town
entries.storyHtml: Closing out the article is Cityview Residence, a small 3-star residence of about 33–35 rooms on Surasak Sa-nguan road, in the centre of Sriracha town, open since 2017. Its Trip.com score is 8.3 from 19 reviews — a smaller sample than the others in this article — but on TripAdvisor it has 4.8 out of 5, ranked #2 of 12 small stays in Sriracha, which shows that people who've actually stayed are happy with it. What reviews bring up most is a pleasant surprise — many say "the inside looks better than the outside of the building": clean rooms, comfortable beds, ice-cold air-con, and especially a bathroom and shower nicer than the price, which Thai-language reviews call a "fancy showerhead". There's a range from Superior up to an upper-floor Deluxe with a Jacuzzi tub in the bathroom, and a with-Balcony room with a roomy balcony worth sitting on. What pleases drivers is the free private parking, hard to come by in central Sriracha, along with a free station shuttle, a rooftop terrace for evening town views, and a Thai-Japanese-American buffet breakfast at around ฿159 a head, which is more varied than you'd expect from a small stay. The location is about a 15-minute walk to Pacific Park, near Surasak Montri Park and the Koh Loy bridge. Honest caveats from the reviews: some rooms have a smell from the drain or drainage that isn't great; the Wi-Fi signal is weak in spots; the breakfast choices are fairly few compared with a big-hotel buffet; there aren't many restaurants within walking distance right by the stay; and some reviews mention the occasional sign of insects. It's best for anyone who wants a clean room, good value, free parking and a central location on a budget, more than anyone who needs a pool or a flawless room in every corner.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if the bathroom matters to you, check the room's condition when you get the key, both the drain smell and the drainage, and if something's not okay tell the team to move you or fix it right away. For a special room, try an upper-floor Deluxe with a Jacuzzi tub or a room with a balcony. If you need the internet for serious work, have a backup plan with a mobile data package.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about budget stays in Sriracha

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best budget stay in Sriracha?
faq.a: It depends on your reason for coming. If you go by overall score and want a roomy room with a kitchen, Racha Residence, with a score of 8.7, is the highest in the article, from over 634 reviews. If you go by the number of reviews and cleanliness, Triple B Boutique Residence has the most reviews at over 1,300 and is walkable to Robinson. If you want to sleep right by the sea with a Koh Loy view, Seaview Sriracha Hotel. If you're on the tightest budget, Benri starts at ฿650 with a soaking tub. And if you want free parking and a nice bathroom, Cityview Residence.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays in Sriracha cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at around ฿650–900 per night. The cheapest end is Benri from ฿650 and Triple B from ฿800; Seaview and Cityview from ฿850; and Racha Residence from ฿900 (a two-bedroom Executive up to around ฿2,200). All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard room; over weekends, long weekends and periods with events in the estates prices may be higher than usual, so compare 3 sites before booking.

faq.q: ❓ Which stay in Sriracha suits a long-stay worker in the estates / Laem Chabang?
faq.a: The residence- and apartment-style stays in this article are designed to suit long stays well. Racha Residence has a kitchenette in every room, good for cooking your own meals. Triple B has a monthly rate from around ฿7,000/month. Benri has rooms with a kitchenette and monthly stays to ask about. All three are walkable to malls and restaurants and within a convenient drive of the port and the Laem Chabang industrial estate.

faq.q: ❓ Do budget stays in Sriracha have a pool?
faq.a: Most don't have a pool, since they're budget in-town stays. In this article only Triple B Boutique Residence has a rooftop pool, but it's small, better for a soak and a chill than serious swimming. Racha Residence has a rooftop and gym but no pool, while Seaview, Benri and Cityview have no pool. If you really need a large pool or a beachfront resort, consider a stay in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead.

faq.q: ❓ What is there to do when you stay in Sriracha?
faq.a: In Sriracha town you can stroll at Koh Loy and the Koh Loy bridge, a seafront sunset spot, eat fresh seafood, and visit Surasak Montri Park. The town is a large Japanese community, so there are ramen shops, izakaya and sushi to hunt down. From Sriracha you can take the boat to Koh Sichang on a morning-to-evening day trip, take a short drive to Khao Kheow Open Zoo and Sriracha Tiger Zoo, and Pattaya is about 20–30 minutes away.

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should I book a stay in Sriracha?
faq.a: Most of the stays in this article are small (10–100 rooms, some just around 10–35), so they fill up fast at certain times. The periods to book ahead for are long weekends, the Kong Khao festival on Koh Loy in late April, and periods with events in the industrial estates — book about 2–4 weeks ahead. In normal periods 1–2 weeks is enough. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a price like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com to get the best price.
